result.title: TSRL: Trigger-based Supervised Reinforcement Learning for Continual Agent Training
result.summary: Large language model (LLM) agents excel at complex, multi-step tasks but suffer from catastrophic forgetting during continual learning--acquiring new skills often degrades previously mastered capabilities. Existing post-training paradigms face a fundamental trade-off: Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) is sample-efficient but prone to severe forgetting, while Reinforcement Learning (RL) preserves prior capabilities but converges slowly without expert guidance. To bridge this gap, we introduce Trigger-based Supervised Reinforcement Learning (TSRL), a framework that integrates the strengths of both paradigms through an adaptive, state-dependent expert supervision mechanism. TSRL employs RL as the optimization backbone, activating SFT selectively on "hard states" where the policy fails. Theoretically, we show that restricting supervision to failure states derives an upper bound on the cumulative parameter updates, thereby reducing forgetting compared to full SFT. Empirically, TSRL achieves consistent gains across three agent benchmarks (ALFWorld, WebShop, and Deep Search) at both 7B and 32B scales. In continual learning scenarios, our method retains up to 9.6 points more capability on prior tasks than SFT->RL baselines, while matching or exceeding target-task performance.

AI.brief_summary: 提出 TSRL 框架：以 RL 为优化主干，仅在策略失败的「hard states」上触发 SFT 监督，以缓解 LLM agent 持续训练中的灾难性遗忘，并在 ALFWorld、WebShop、Deep Search 上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按状态触发、选择性施加专家监督」的机制可能为 LVR 中何时注入监督或额外计算、以及轨迹训练的贡献分配提供可供核查的线索；但论文属纯文本 agent 持续学习，未涉及视觉证据或 latent 推理状态。
